{{Legend0|#D3D3D3|No election}} }} '''United States gubernatorial elections''' are scheduled to be held on November 7, 2028, in the states of [[Delaware]], [[Indiana]], [[Missouri]], [[Montana]], [[North Carolina]], [[North Dakota]], [[Utah]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]], [[West Virginia]], [[New Hampshire]], and [[Vermont]]. These elections form part of the [[2028 United States elections]]. The last regular gubernatorial elections for nine of these states were in [[2024 United States gubernatorial elections|2024]]. The governors of New Hampshire and Vermont are elected to two year terms and were last elected in [[2026 United States gubernatorial elections|2026]]. Republicans are defending two governorships in states [[Kamala Harris]] won in [[2024 United States presidential election|2024]], while [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] are defending one governorship in a state Donald Trump won in 2024. == Race summary == === States === {| class="wikitable sortable" |- valign=bottom ! He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. == Indiana == {{Main|2028 Indiana gubernatorial election}} Governor [[Mike Braun]] was elected in [[2024 Indiana gubernatorial election|2024]] with 54.38% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election.{{Cite web |title=Mike Braun gets back to executive roots with jump to Indiana governor |url=https://www.brauntransition.com/2024/12/11/mike-braun-gets-back-to-executive-roots-with-jump-to-indiana-governor/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |language=en-US|date=December 11, 2024|website=Braun Transition|last=Sivak|first=David}} He announced his candidacy on November 16, 2026.{{cite web |last1=Maurer |first1=Sam |title=Indiana Governor Mike Braun announces reelection bid |url=https://fox59.com/news/indiana-governor-mike-braun-announced-reelection-bid/ |website=Fox 59 Indianapolis |access-date=17 November 2026}} [[Indiana Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[Todd Rokita]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Indiana|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Micah Beckwith]] are seen as potential primary opponents to Braun.{{Cite web |last=Dweyer |first=Kayla |date=November 10, 2026 |title=Gov. Braun to announce reelection bid; will he draw a challenger? |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/news/politics/2026/11/10/gov-braun-to-announce-reelection-bid-will-he-draw-a-challenger/92707244007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=false&gca-epti=z113729p003650l117450c003650u113629e1195xxv113729&gca-ft=224&gca-ds=sophi |access-date=November 10, 2026 |website=Indy Star |publisher=Indy Star}} {{Cite web |last=Throp |first=Benjamin |date=November 10, 2026 |title=AG Rokita calls on Braun to discipline teachers who made comments about Charlie Kirk |url=https://www.wfyi.org/statewide/2026-11-10/ag-rokita-calls-on-braun-to-discipline-teachers-who-made-comments-about-charlie-kirk |url-status=live |archive-date=November 10, 2026 |access-date=November 10, 2026 |website=WFYI |publisher=WFYI|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261110222139/https://www.wfyi.org/statewide/2026-11-10/ag-rokita-calls-on-braun-to-discipline-teachers-who-made-comments-about-charlie-kirk}}{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Mike |last2=Almanza |first2=Alex |date=November 16, 2026 |title='Never been more fired up' {{!}} Indiana Gov. Mike Braun announces re-election bid for 2028 |url=https://www.wthr.com/article/news/politics/indiana-gov-mike-braun-announces-re-election-bid-for-2028-governor-rokita-beckwith-bayh-primary-republican-democrat-race-announcement/531-92c60f60-c3e9-472e-a288-4d6e94eaa6f3 |website=13 WTHR}} == Missouri == Governor [[Mike Kehoe]] was elected in [[2024 Missouri gubernatorial election|2024]] with 59.14% of the vote. He is running for re-election to a second term.{{cite news |last=Wardynski |first=Jack |title=Gov. Kehoe announces intention to run for second term in 2028 |work=[[News Tribune (Jefferson City)|Jefferson City News Tribune]] |url=https://www.newstribune.com/news/2026/jun/24/gov-kehoe-announces-intention-to-run-for-second/ |date=June 24, 2026}} Former [[Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation|Co-Deputy Director of the FBI]] and [[Missouri Attorney General]] [[Andrew Bailey (politician)|Andrew Bailey]] is seen as a potential primary opponent to Kehoe.{{Cite web |last=Rosenbaum |first=Jason |date=2026-10-06 |title=After heading home to Missouri, Andrew Bailey isn’t ruling out another run for office |url=https://www.stlpr.org/government-politics-issues/2026-10-06/after-heading-home-to-missouri-andrew-bailey-isnt-ruling-out-another-run-for-office |access-date=2026-11-23 |website=STLPR |language=en}} Kansas City mayor [[Quinton Lucas]], who will be term-limited in his current position in 2027, has formed an exploratory committee as a potential Democratic candidate.{{cite news |last=Higginbotham |first=Abbey |title=Mayor Quinton Lucas takes a step toward governor run |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |url=https://www.axios.com/local/kansas-city/2026/11/19/quinton-lucas-missouri-governor-2028-exploratory-committee |date=Nov 19, 2026}} == Montana == Governor [[Greg Gianforte]] was re-elected in [[2024 Montana gubernatorial election|2024]] with 58.86% of the vote. He will be [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] by the [[Constitution of Montana]] and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. [[Montana Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[Austin Knudsen]], [[United States Representative]] [[Troy Downing]], and [[Lieutenant Governor of Montana|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Kristen Juras]] are all seen as potential Republican candidates. Meanwhile, [[2024 Montana gubernatorial election|2024]] Democratic nominee for governor Ryan Busse, Democratic nominee for [[Montana's 1st congressional district|MT-01]] in [[2022 United States House of Representatives election in Montana|2022]] and [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana|2024]] [[Monica Tranel]], and former chief legal counsel to Governor [[Steve Bullock (American politician)|Steve Bullock]] [[Raph Graybill]] are all seen as potential Democratic candidates.{{cite web |last1=Knox |first1=Jim |title=Montana Candidate & Election Guide |url=https://politics1.com/mt.htm|date=November 4, 2026|website=Politics1}} == New Hampshire == Governor [[Kelly Ayotte]] was re-elected to a second term in [[2026 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2026]] with 51.43% of the vote. Because [[New Hampshire]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[New Hampshire Constitution|Constitution]], she will be eligible to run for re-election for a third term. == North Carolina == {{Main|2028 North Carolina gubernatorial election}} Governor [[Josh Stein]] was elected in [[2024 North Carolina gubernatorial election|2024]] with 54.90% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. Robert Burns, the Republican mayor of [[Monroe, North Carolina|Monroe]], announced his candidacy on November 18, 2026.{{cite web |title=Monroe mayor announces bid for North Carolina governor |url=https://www.wsoctv.com/news/local/monroe-mayor-announces-bid-north-carolina-governor/Z75PQBVMWNA3XFKKXY5RW6HD6M/ |website=[[WSOC-TV]] |access-date=2026-11-18|date=November 18, 2026|last=Esposito|first=Gina}} [[North Carolina State Auditor|State Auditor]] [[Dave Boliek]] is also seen as a potential candidate.{{cite web |title=Is 2028 Dave Boliek's moment? |url=https://www.longleafpol.com/p/dave-boliek-governor-2028 |website=Longleaf Politics |access-date=2026-05-28|date=September 8, 2025|last=Dunn|first=Andrew}} == North Dakota == Governor [[Kelly Armstrong]] was elected in [[2024 North Dakota gubernatorial election|2024]] with 68.26% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. == Utah == Governor [[Spencer Cox]] was re-elected in [[2024 Utah gubernatorial election|2024]] with 52.89% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has stated he will not. [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[John Curtis]] and former [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Jason Chaffetz]] have both expressed interest in a possible campaign.{{Cite web |last=Benson |first=Samuel |date=2026-05-11 |title=Sen. John Curtis exploring 2028 run for Utah governor |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/11/sen-john-curtis-exploring-2028-run-for-utah-governor-00913981 |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en-US}} Other potential candidates include [[Utah House of Representatives|Utah House]] Speaker [[Mike Schultz (politician)|Mike Schultz]], [[Lieutenant Governor of Utah|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Deidre Henderson]], U.S. Representative [[Blake Moore]], and businessmen Jeremy Andrus and Brad Bonham.{{Cite web |last=Tomco |first=Brigham |last2= |first2= |date=2026-05-13 |title=Inside the 'shadow primary' for Utah governor |url=https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/05/13/utah-republican-race-for-governor-in-2028-might-already-come-down-to-jason-chaffetz-and-john-curtis/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Deseret News |language=en}} == Vermont == Governor [[Phil Scott]] was re-elected to a sixth term in [[2026 Vermont gubernatorial election|2026]] with 52.43% of the vote. Because [[Vermont]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[Vermont Constitution|Constitution]], he will be eligible to run in 2028 for a seventh term. == Washington == Governor [[Bob Ferguson (politician)|Bob Ferguson]] was elected in [[2024 Washington gubernatorial election|2024]] with 55.51% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. [[Washington House of Representatives|State Representative]] and Chair of the [[Washington State Republican Party]] [[Jim Walsh (Washington politician)|Jim Walsh]] has expressed interest in running.{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-06-03 |title='Of course I'm looking at it:' Walsh eyes a run for governor |url=https://chinookobserver.com/2026/06/03/of-course-im-looking-at-it-walsh-eyes-a-run-for-governor/ |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=Chinook Observer |language=en}} [[Washington State Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction|State Superintendent of Public Instruction]] [[Chris Reykdal]] is seen as a potential [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] challenger to Bob Ferguson after saying he would not run for a fourth term as superintendent in 2028.{{Cite web |last=Nir |first=David |date=2026-11-13 |title=Morning Digest, sponsored by Civitech: A trio of governors could face tough opposition from their own party |url=https://www.the-downballot.com/p/morning-digest-sponsored-by-civitech |access-date=2026-11-13 |website=The Downballot |language=en}} == West Virginia == {{Main|2028 West Virginia gubernatorial election}} Governor [[Patrick Morrisey]] was elected in [[2024 West Virginia gubernatorial election|2024]] with 61.99% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. Former governor and [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Jim Justice]] and former governor and Senator [[Joe Manchin]] are seen as potential candidates.{{Cite web |last=Meadows |first=T. J. |date=2026-08-21 |title=Justice Has a Decision to Make |url=https://wvmetronews.com/2026/08/21/justice-has-a-decision-to-make/ |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=WV MetroNews |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Charles |date=2026-09-04 |title=Joe Manchin says West Virginia needs ‘new talent’ as Justice weighs 2028 run |url=https://www.wvnews.com/news/wvnews/joe-manchin-says-west-virginia-needs-new-talent-as-justice-weighs-2028-run/article_0260904b-955e-499c-bfd2-97815b212e97.html |access-date=2026-11-13 |website=WV News |language=en}} [[Secretary of State of West Virginia|Secretary of State]] [[Kris Warner]] and [[West Virginia State Treasurer|State Treasurer]] [[Larry Pack]] are also rumored to be candidates.{{Cite web |title=Reporter’s Notebook: Blood in the water |url=https://www.newsandsentinel.com/opinion/local-columns/2026/10/reporters-notebook-blood-in-the-water/ |access-date=November 13, 2026 |website=News and Sentinel |language=en-US|date=October 12, 2026}} == Territories == === American Samoa === Governor [[Pula Nikolao Pula]] was elected in [[2024 American Samoan general election|2024]] with 59.83% of the vote in a runoff. He is eligible to run for re-election and has expressed interest in doing so.{{cite news|title = Governor: I am prepared to go to the Fono|url = https://www.talanei.com/2026/04/01/governor-i-am-prepared-to-go-to-the-fono/|website = Talanei|date = April 1, 2026|access-date = November 5, 2026|quote = ... his intention to run for re-election in 2028.}} === Puerto Rico === Governor [[Jenniffer González-Colón]] was elected in [[2024 Puerto Rico gubernatorial election|2024]] with 41.22% of the vote. She is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if she will do so. == Notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} {{2028 United States elections}} {{United States gubernatorial elections}} [[Category:2028 United States gubernatorial elections| ]] [[Category:2028 elections in the United States]]

{{Legend0|#D3D3D3|No election}} }} '''United States gubernatorial elections''' are scheduled to be held on November 7, 2028, in the states of [[Delaware]], [[Indiana]], [[Missouri]], [[Montana]], [[North Carolina]], [[North Dakota]], [[Utah]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]], [[West Virginia]], [[New Hampshire]], and [[Vermont]]. These elections form part of the [[2028 United States elections]]. The last regular gubernatorial elections for nine of these states were in [[2024 United States gubernatorial elections|2024]]. The governors of New Hampshire and Vermont are elected to two year terms and were last elected in [[2026 United States gubernatorial elections|2026]]. Republicans are defending two governorships in states [[Kamala Harris]] won in [[2024 United States presidential election|2024]], while [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] are defending one governorship in a state Donald Trump won in 2024. == Race summary == === States === {| class="wikitable sortable" |- valign=bottom ! He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. == Indiana == {{Main|2028 Indiana gubernatorial election}} Governor [[Mike Braun]] was elected in [[2024 Indiana gubernatorial election|2024]] with 54.38% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election.{{Cite web |title=Mike Braun gets back to executive roots with jump to Indiana governor |url=https://www.brauntransition.com/2024/12/11/mike-braun-gets-back-to-executive-roots-with-jump-to-indiana-governor/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |language=en-US|date=December 11, 2024|website=Braun Transition|last=Sivak|first=David}} He announced his candidacy on November 16, 2026.{{cite web |last1=Maurer |first1=Sam |title=Indiana Governor Mike Braun announces reelection bid |url=https://fox59.com/news/indiana-governor-mike-braun-announced-reelection-bid/ |website=Fox 59 Indianapolis |access-date=17 November 2026}} [[Indiana Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[Todd Rokita]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Indiana|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Micah Beckwith]] are seen as potential primary opponents to Braun.{{Cite web |last=Dweyer |first=Kayla |date=November 10, 2026 |title=Gov. Braun to announce reelection bid; will he draw a challenger? |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/news/politics/2026/11/10/gov-braun-to-announce-reelection-bid-will-he-draw-a-challenger/92707244007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=false&gca-epti=z113729p003650l117450c003650u113629e1195xxv113729&gca-ft=224&gca-ds=sophi |access-date=November 10, 2026 |website=Indy Star |publisher=Indy Star}} {{Cite web |last=Throp |first=Benjamin |date=November 10, 2026 |title=AG Rokita calls on Braun to discipline teachers who made comments about Charlie Kirk |url=https://www.wfyi.org/statewide/2026-11-10/ag-rokita-calls-on-braun-to-discipline-teachers-who-made-comments-about-charlie-kirk |url-status=live |archive-date=November 10, 2026 |access-date=November 10, 2026 |website=WFYI |publisher=WFYI|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261110222139/https://www.wfyi.org/statewide/2026-11-10/ag-rokita-calls-on-braun-to-discipline-teachers-who-made-comments-about-charlie-kirk}}{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Mike |last2=Almanza |first2=Alex |date=November 16, 2026 |title='Never been more fired up' {{!}} Indiana Gov. Mike Braun announces re-election bid for 2028 |url=https://www.wthr.com/article/news/politics/indiana-gov-mike-braun-announces-re-election-bid-for-2028-governor-rokita-beckwith-bayh-primary-republican-democrat-race-announcement/531-92c60f60-c3e9-472e-a288-4d6e94eaa6f3 |website=13 WTHR}} == Missouri == Governor [[Mike Kehoe]] was elected in [[2024 Missouri gubernatorial election|2024]] with 59.14% of the vote. He is running for re-election to a second term.{{cite news |last=Wardynski |first=Jack |title=Gov. Kehoe announces intention to run for second term in 2028 |work=[[News Tribune (Jefferson City)|Jefferson City News Tribune]] |url=https://www.newstribune.com/news/2026/jun/24/gov-kehoe-announces-intention-to-run-for-second/ |date=June 24, 2026}} Former [[Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation|Co-Deputy Director of the FBI]] and [[Missouri Attorney General]] [[Andrew Bailey (politician)|Andrew Bailey]] is seen as a potential primary opponent to Kehoe.{{Cite web |last=Rosenbaum |first=Jason |date=2026-10-06 |title=After heading home to Missouri, Andrew Bailey isn’t ruling out another run for office |url=https://www.stlpr.org/government-politics-issues/2026-10-06/after-heading-home-to-missouri-andrew-bailey-isnt-ruling-out-another-run-for-office |access-date=2026-11-23 |website=STLPR |language=en}} Kansas City mayor [[Quinton Lucas]], who will be term-limited in his current position in 2027, has formed an exploratory committee as a potential Democratic candidate.{{cite news |last=Higginbotham |first=Abbey |title=Mayor Quinton Lucas takes a step toward governor run |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |url=https://www.axios.com/local/kansas-city/2026/11/19/quinton-lucas-missouri-governor-2028-exploratory-committee |date=Nov 19, 2026}} == Montana == Governor [[Greg Gianforte]] was re-elected in [[2024 Montana gubernatorial election|2024]] with 58.86% of the vote. He will be [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] by the [[Constitution of Montana]] and cannot seek re-election to a third consecutive term. [[Montana Attorney General|Attorney General]] [[Austin Knudsen]], [[United States Representative]] [[Troy Downing]], and [[Lieutenant Governor of Montana|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Kristen Juras]] are all seen as potential Republican candidates. Meanwhile, [[2024 Montana gubernatorial election|2024]] Democratic nominee for governor Ryan Busse, Democratic nominee for [[Montana's 1st congressional district|MT-01]] in [[2022 United States House of Representatives election in Montana|2022]] and [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana|2024]] [[Monica Tranel]], and former chief legal counsel to Governor [[Steve Bullock (American politician)|Steve Bullock]] [[Raph Graybill]] are all seen as potential Democratic candidates.{{cite web |last1=Knox |first1=Jim |title=Montana Candidate & Election Guide |url=https://politics1.com/mt.htm|date=November 4, 2026|website=Politics1}} == New Hampshire == Governor [[Kelly Ayotte]] was re-elected to a second term in [[2026 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2026]] with 51.43% of the vote. Because [[New Hampshire]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[New Hampshire Constitution|Constitution]], she will be eligible to run for re-election for a third term. == North Carolina == {{Main|2028 North Carolina gubernatorial election}} Governor [[Josh Stein]] was elected in [[2024 North Carolina gubernatorial election|2024]] with 54.90% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. Robert Burns, the Republican mayor of [[Monroe, North Carolina|Monroe]], announced his candidacy on November 18, 2026.{{cite web |title=Monroe mayor announces bid for North Carolina governor |url=https://www.wsoctv.com/news/local/monroe-mayor-announces-bid-north-carolina-governor/Z75PQBVMWNA3XFKKXY5RW6HD6M/ |website=[[WSOC-TV]] |access-date=2026-11-18|date=November 18, 2026|last=Esposito|first=Gina}} [[North Carolina State Auditor|State Auditor]] [[Dave Boliek]] is also seen as a potential candidate.{{cite web |title=Is 2028 Dave Boliek's moment? |url=https://www.longleafpol.com/p/dave-boliek-governor-2028 |website=Longleaf Politics |access-date=2026-05-28|date=September 8, 2025|last=Dunn|first=Andrew}} == North Dakota == Governor [[Kelly Armstrong]] was elected in [[2024 North Dakota gubernatorial election|2024]] with 68.26% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. == Utah == Governor [[Spencer Cox]] was re-elected in [[2024 Utah gubernatorial election|2024]] with 52.89% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has stated he will not. [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[John Curtis]] and former [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Jason Chaffetz]] have both expressed interest in a possible campaign.{{Cite web |last=Benson |first=Samuel |date=2026-05-11 |title=Sen. John Curtis exploring 2028 run for Utah governor |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/11/sen-john-curtis-exploring-2028-run-for-utah-governor-00913981 |access-date=2026-05-11 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en-US}} Other potential candidates include [[Utah House of Representatives|Utah House]] Speaker [[Mike Schultz (politician)|Mike Schultz]], [[Lieutenant Governor of Utah|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Deidre Henderson]], U.S. Representative [[Blake Moore]], and businessmen Jeremy Andrus and Brad Bonham.{{Cite web |last=Tomco |first=Brigham |last2= |first2= |date=2026-05-13 |title=Inside the 'shadow primary' for Utah governor |url=https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/05/13/utah-republican-race-for-governor-in-2028-might-already-come-down-to-jason-chaffetz-and-john-curtis/ |access-date=2026-05-14 |website=Deseret News |language=en}} == Vermont == Governor [[Phil Scott]] was re-elected to a sixth term in [[2026 Vermont gubernatorial election|2026]] with 52.43% of the vote. Because [[Vermont]] does not have gubernatorial term limits in its [[Vermont Constitution|Constitution]], he will be eligible to run in 2028 for a seventh term. == Washington == Governor [[Bob Ferguson (politician)|Bob Ferguson]] was elected in [[2024 Washington gubernatorial election|2024]] with 55.51% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. [[Washington House of Representatives|State Representative]] and Chair of the [[Washington State Republican Party]] [[Jim Walsh (Washington politician)|Jim Walsh]] has expressed interest in running.{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-06-03 |title='Of course I'm looking at it:' Walsh eyes a run for governor |url=https://chinookobserver.com/2026/06/03/of-course-im-looking-at-it-walsh-eyes-a-run-for-governor/ |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=Chinook Observer |language=en}} [[Washington State Office of Superintendent of Public Instruction|State Superintendent of Public Instruction]] [[Chris Reykdal]] is seen as a potential [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] challenger to Bob Ferguson after saying he would not run for a fourth term as superintendent in 2028.{{Cite web |last=Nir |first=David |date=2026-11-13 |title=Morning Digest, sponsored by Civitech: A trio of governors could face tough opposition from their own party |url=https://www.the-downballot.com/p/morning-digest-sponsored-by-civitech |access-date=2026-11-13 |website=The Downballot |language=en}} == West Virginia == {{Main|2028 West Virginia gubernatorial election}} Governor [[Patrick Morrisey]] was elected in [[2024 West Virginia gubernatorial election|2024]] with 61.99% of the vote. He is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if he will do so. Former governor and [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Jim Justice]] and former governor and Senator [[Joe Manchin]] are seen as potential candidates.{{Cite web |last=Meadows |first=T. J. |date=2026-08-21 |title=Justice Has a Decision to Make |url=https://wvmetronews.com/2026/08/21/justice-has-a-decision-to-make/ |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=WV MetroNews |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Charles |date=2026-09-04 |title=Joe Manchin says West Virginia needs ‘new talent’ as Justice weighs 2028 run |url=https://www.wvnews.com/news/wvnews/joe-manchin-says-west-virginia-needs-new-talent-as-justice-weighs-2028-run/article_0260904b-955e-499c-bfd2-97815b212e97.html |access-date=2026-11-13 |website=WV News |language=en}} [[Secretary of State of West Virginia|Secretary of State]] [[Kris Warner]] and [[West Virginia State Treasurer|State Treasurer]] [[Larry Pack]] are also rumored to be candidates.{{Cite web |title=Reporter’s Notebook: Blood in the water |url=https://www.newsandsentinel.com/opinion/local-columns/2026/10/reporters-notebook-blood-in-the-water/ |access-date=November 13, 2026 |website=News and Sentinel |language=en-US|date=October 12, 2026}} == Territories == === American Samoa === Governor [[Pula Nikolao Pula]] was elected in [[2024 American Samoan general election|2024]] with 59.83% of the vote in a runoff. He is eligible to run for re-election and has expressed interest in doing so.{{cite news|title = Governor: I am prepared to go to the Fono|url = https://www.talanei.com/2026/04/01/governor-i-am-prepared-to-go-to-the-fono/|website = Talanei|date = April 1, 2026|access-date = November 5, 2026|quote = ... his intention to run for re-election in 2028.}} === Puerto Rico === Governor [[Jenniffer González-Colón]] was elected in [[2024 Puerto Rico gubernatorial election|2024]] with 41.22% of the vote. She is eligible to run for re-election but has not yet stated if she will do so. == Notes == {{Notelist}} == References == {{Reflist}} {{2028 United States elections}} {{United States gubernatorial elections}} [[Category:2028 United States gubernatorial elections| ]] [[Category:2028 elections in the United States]]
